objectives.wording: Map organelles and signalling pathways to cell functions and interpret a clinical or research example.
Draw a regulated variable's feedback loop and predict its response to a disturbance.
Compare intrinsic and extrinsic pathways and explain the role of programmed death in tissue maintenance.
Classify transport mechanisms by energy source and gradient and predict flux in representative examples.
Compare compartment volumes and ions and select tracers to estimate compartment sizes.
Use a buffer equation to explain how bicarbonate and other buffers oppose changes in pH.
Relate ion gradients and permeability to resting potential and trace channel changes during a nerve action potential.
Relate plasma and formed elements to transport, defence and haemostasis.
Compare their origins, fractions and functions and explain clinical consequences of representative changes.
Trace synthesis and breakdown, relate structure to gas transport and compare clinically important variants.
Using approved specimens or simulations, estimate haemoglobin concentration.
Trace maturation and explain how oxygen delivery and erythropoietin regulate red cell production in health and disease.
Explain the physiological mechanisms of anaemia and the physiological principles of its management.
Explain the physiological mechanisms of polycythaemia and the physiological principles of its management.
Explain the physiological mechanisms of jaundice and the physiological principles of its management.
Trace leucocyte production and compare the regulation, structure and functions of the major cell types.
Compare innate and adaptive responses and explain their development, regulation and protective roles.
Trace megakaryocyte maturation and platelet release, then explain platelet structure, function and causes of count variation.
Trace platelet plug formation and coagulation, identify anticoagulant targets and contrast mechanisms of representative bleeding and thrombotic disorders.
Discuss the types of blood groups and the clinical importance of blood grouping.
Using approved specimens or simulations, determine the ABO and Rh blood group.
Discuss blood banking and blood transfusion, including the physiological basis of transfusion reactions.
Using approved specimens or simulations, perform a red blood cell count.
Using approved specimens or simulations, perform total and differential leucocyte counts.
Using approved specimens or simulations, determine bleeding time and clotting time.
Calculate red cell indices from measured haemoglobin, haematocrit and red cell count.
Describe how ESR is measured and interpret its findings.
Describe how red cell osmotic fragility is tested and interpret its findings.
Describe how haematocrit is measured and interpret its findings.
Describe the steps of a reticulocyte count.
Describe the steps of a platelet count.
Describe the structure and functions of a neuron and discuss nerve growth factors.
Describe the structure and functions of neuroglia.
Compare nerve fibre classes and derive rheobase and chronaxie from a strength-duration curve.
Classify injury patterns and predict degeneration and regeneration from the structures involved.
Diagram the junction and trace events from motor nerve depolarization to the muscle action potential.
Explain the postsynaptic neuromuscular transmission defect in myasthenia gravis and how blocking agents affect it.
Explain the presynaptic neuromuscular transmission defect in Lambert-Eaton syndrome and contrast it with myasthenia gravis.
Compare representative fibre types by structure and function and explain the ionic basis of their electrical activity.
Trace excitation-contraction coupling from membrane depolarization to cross-bridge cycling and relate it to muscle properties.
Explain electrical and calcium signalling, calmodulin-dependent activation and the basis of sustained force.
Compare isometric and isotonic contractions, identify energy sources and explain how recruitment and firing rate grade force.
Group representative myopathies by mechanism and relate them to impaired muscle function.
Record contractions against a known load and calculate external work from the measured displacement.
Observe nerve-muscle and cardiac experiments in a computer simulation and explain the recorded responses to representative interventions.
Map digestive organs and wall layers to motility, secretion and absorption.
Match major gastrointestinal hormones to their release stimuli, targets and feedback effects.
Trace acinar secretion and ductal modification and explain how flow and autonomic input change saliva.
